narrative: Material PL2__MCB48083 exhibits stable low-variability demand (CV=0.197) over 132 working days, with a mean daily demand of 116,513 units. Lead times are volatile (CV=0.596, mean=1.56 days), driven primarily by transport variability, which necessitates a substantial safety stock of 184,059 units to achieve the 95% service level. The classical EOQ (r,Q) model is selected as the optimal replenishment policy: it consolidates 2,563 annual MOQ orders into 49 large replenishments of 589,557 units each, reducing total annual inventory cost by 94.9% from $192,008 to $9,725 while keeping total stock within the 843,693-unit storage cap.

research_insights.selected_model: EOQ with safety stock — (r, Q) continuous-review policy
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is stable and low-variability (CV=0.197) with 100% non-zero days, making continuous-review EOQ the textbook-optimal choice. The normal approximation for safety stock is appropriate given the near-normal demand distribution confirmed by histogram inspection.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Lead time variability (CV=0.596) is classified as unstable. The safety stock formula explicitly accounts for both demand and lead time variance via sigma_ltd. Total inventory post-replenishment (773,616 units) is 91.7% of the storage cap — feasible but approaching the ceiling; any upward revision to safety stock should be reviewed against capacity.
